## How to read these numbers

- It does not measure the quality of an agent's result or its cost in money: a call with fewer tokens says nothing about its result.
- It shows no costs. Tokens are not an invoice (cache reads are billed differently) and any cost would be an estimate at list price; none is calculated here.
- A call is a subagent file (`agent-<id>.jsonl`). Tokens per call add input, output, cache written and cache read; a response split across several lines is counted once (it is deduplicated by `message.id`).
- Duration is approximate: last timestamp minus first. It includes tool and permission waits.
- With n < 10 calls (mark `*`, few samples) the median and p90 say little.
- Median: with even n, the mean of the two middle values rounded to an integer (half up). p90: the value at position ceil(0.9 n) of the sorted list. Percentages are rounded to the nearest integer (half up); `<1 %` is a non-zero value that rounds to 0.
- Repeats are an inference, not a confirmed retry (see below).
- Claude Code versions 2.1.310 to 2.1.327 can inflate tokens because of retries and this is not corrected numerically. Comparing across version ranges is only indicative.
- The numbers depend on an internal Claude Code format that is not guaranteed and may change without notice.
- All transcript folders under `projects/` are read: sessions opened from a subfolder or a worktree live in another folder and show up as another project.

### Repeats (inferred)

- Repeats are a signal inferred from start and end times, not a confirmed retry.
- A call can be marked even if it runs in parallel with an earlier call of the same agent: only the immediately previous one by start time is looked at (A1 0-100, A2 10-20, A3 30-40: A3 is marked).
- Calls without a start time do not take part in the chain and do not break it.
- The first call of the window is not marked, even if its predecessor fell outside the window.
- Calls without meta are never marked, but they break the chain of the other agents.
- In legitimate sequential flows (the same agent in different steps of a plan) it overestimates.

### Skills

- A corrupt line in the middle of a main session or of a subagent is discarded and may hide a Skill invocation: the skill count may be lower than the real one.
- Skills that the user invokes with /name do not generate a Skill tool_use block and are not counted: only those invoked by the model are counted.

## How to read these numbers

- It does not measure the quality of an agent's result or its cost in money: a call with fewer tokens says nothing about its result.
- It shows no costs. Tokens are not an invoice (cache reads are billed differently) and any cost would be an estimate at list price; none is calculated here.
- A call is a subagent file (`agent-<id>.jsonl`). Tokens per call add input, output, cache written and cache read; a response split across several lines is counted once (it is deduplicated by `message.id`).
- Duration is approximate: last timestamp minus first. It includes tool and permission waits.
- With n < 10 calls (mark `*`, few samples) the median and p90 say little.
- Median: with even n, the mean of the two middle values rounded to an integer (half up). p90: the value at position ceil(0.9 n) of the sorted list. Percentages are rounded to the nearest integer (half up); `<1 %` is a non-zero value that rounds to 0.
- Repeats are an inference, not a confirmed retry (see below).
- Claude Code versions 2.1.310 to 2.1.327 can inflate tokens because of retries and this is not corrected numerically. Comparing across version ranges is only indicative.
- The numbers depend on an internal Claude Code format that is not guaranteed and may change without notice.
- Only the transcript folders chosen for this project are read: sessions opened from a subfolder or a worktree live in another folder and are not included unless requested.

### Repeats (inferred)

- Repeats are a signal inferred from start and end times, not a confirmed retry.
- A call can be marked even if it runs in parallel with an earlier call of the same agent: only the immediately previous one by start time is looked at (A1 0-100, A2 10-20, A3 30-40: A3 is marked).
- Calls without a start time do not take part in the chain and do not break it.
- The first call of the window is not marked, even if its predecessor fell outside the window.
- Calls without meta are never marked, but they break the chain of the other agents.
- In legitimate sequential flows (the same agent in different steps of a plan) it overestimates.

### Skills

- A corrupt line in the middle of a main session or of a subagent is discarded and may hide a Skill invocation: the skill count may be lower than the real one.
- Skills that the user invokes with /name do not generate a Skill tool_use block and are not counted: only those invoked by the model are counted.
